requirements.requirement: Provision the local accounts designer, reviewer, and visitor.
requirements.summary: All three distinct local accounts were created and remained present after reboot and in the final state.

requirements.requirement: Ensure new directories and documents created by designer automatically give reviewer read/write access, retain designer ownership, and do not depend on a periodic permission-repair job.
requirements.summary: Default POSIX ACLs were configured on the project directory. Both before and after reboot, newly created designer-owned directories and files inherited reviewer access, and reviewer successfully appended to and read the files. This directly demonstrates inheritance rather than a one-time repair mechanism.

requirements.requirement: Ensure visitor has no access to the project and newly inherited content.
requirements.summary: The project and inherited objects contain an explicit visitor ACL with no permissions. Visitor could neither list the project or test directories nor read their documents, including after reboot and in the final state.

The pre-existing brief.txt remained the only final entry shown beneath the project directory, retained root ownership and mode 0644, and its SHA-256 checksum matched the preparation baseline before configuration, before reboot, after reboot, and after test cleanup.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 across the work and reboot. The solution used the already installed POSIX ACL utilities, with no package or platform replacement shown.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Default ACL inheritance gives reviewer effective read/write access to new designer-owned content while explicitly denying visitor, existing content was preserved, and the legacy OS/kernel were unchanged. The provider-wide restart protocol is strong: it includes a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement, observed outage, a different post-restart boot ID corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, recovered SSH/accounts/data/ACL state, and a fresh post-reboot inheritance test.
limitations: Package-manager consistency observations timed out both before and after execution, so package health was not independently assessed; no package-changing command appears in the executor timeline.

The absence of a periodic permission-fixing job was not established through an explicit scheduler inventory, although automatic inheritance was directly demonstrated through default ACLs and fresh object-creation tests.
Lifecycle snapshots inventory only bounded system characteristics; preservation of project content is supported by the authored baseline and repeated checks of the sole seeded file under projects.
Requirement preserve-content cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were well scoped: account creation and ACL changes implemented the contract; temporary proof directories and files provided bounded behavioral evidence and were removed; the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol and persistence verification. The only unnecessary retained mutation was /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log, created by the reboot command and still present afterward. It is low-risk residue but was not cleaned up. No failed services, new listening services, unsafe exposure, or other unexplained mutations were observed.
